findings.condition: The acceptance criterion requires /OUT to be within 0.62-0.65 V at 1 ms after a 1 V step 'while connected to a switched ADC input', but ADC sampling capacitance, switch resistance, initial charge and sampling timing are all unspecified. Unloaded nominal response is 0.63212 V (ngspice measurement), leaving only 12.1 mV margin to the lower bound and 17.9 mV to the upper.

evidence.locator: vout_at_1ms = 6.321204e-01 V, vout_at_2ms = 8.646647e-01 V (ngspice-42 batch run)
margins 12.12/17.88 mV; RL=320k -> 0.6239 V; leakage threshold 1.21 uA; Cs=2 nF -> dV=12.4 mV; dV/dt=0.368 mV/us; time window 0.9676-1.0498 ms
lines 1-2: ADC parameters 'have not been specified'; 'do not invent ADC behavior'

findings.location: inputs/requirements.txt; /OUT net (inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch labels OUT; J1 pad 2)
findings.mechanism: Any real switched-capacitor ADC front end draws charge from the 10 kOhm source node. Bounding calculations: a DC load/leakage of ~1.21 uA at /OUT (equivalently RL <= ~320 kOhm) erodes the full 12.1 mV lower margin; a discharged internal sampling capacitor of ~1.9-2 nF charge-shared with C1 at the sample instant does the same (10-100 pF is negligible, <=0.63 mV); the output is still slewing 0.368 mV/us at 1 ms, so the in-window time interval is only 0.9676-1.0498 ms (-32 us/+50 us around the nominal sample point). None of these parameters is bounded by the candidate or requirements, so loaded compliance cannot be established either way.
findings.reasoning: This is the central scope question. The design passes the criterion nominally and unloaded, but the stated operating condition (connected switched ADC) is unparameterized, and the quantified margins show that plausible magnitudes of ADC loading or sample-timing variation would decide pass/fail. Per the scope's own instruction this is missing coverage rather than an established defect, so it is reported as a major concern, not a defect.
findings.title: Settling criterion under switched ADC load is unverifiable; margins are narrow

findings.condition: Meeting 0.62-0.65 V at exactly 1 ms requires the RC product to lie in [0.9525, 1.0335] ms, i.e. within -4.75%/+3.35% of the nominal 1.000 ms. The schematic specifies only nominal values with no tolerance, dielectric or part-number data.

evidence.locator: RC product must lie in [0.9525, 1.0335] ms => -4.75% .. +3.35% allowed deviation
C1 property Value "100n" (symbol uuid 1dcaf7b4...), R1 property Value "10k" (symbol uuid c5c38e1a...); no tolerance properties present

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (R1 Value '10k', C1 Value '100n'; no tolerance fields)
findings.mechanism: V(1 ms) = 1 - exp(-1 ms/RC). Solving the window bounds gives the allowed RC range. Common 100 nF ceramic capacitors carry +/-10% (sometimes +/-5%) tolerance before temperature and DC-bias effects, which alone exceeds the +3.35% / -4.75% budget; a +/-1% resistor adds further spread. With no tolerance specification in the candidate, compliance is guaranteed only for exactly-nominal parts.
findings.reasoning: No tolerance requirement is stated, so I do not assert a violation; but the window implied by the stated criterion is tighter than typical off-the-shelf capacitor tolerance, and the candidate contains no data showing the parts selected can hold it. Flagged as a minor concern / coverage gap rather than a defect, consistent with 'do not impose unstated ratings'.
findings.title: No component tolerances stated; criterion window allows only -4.75%/+3.35% RC deviation

findings.condition: The unloaded step response does not settle in the 0.62-0.65 V band: it passes through it near t=1 ms and continues to 0.8647 V at 2 ms and 1.0 V asymptotically. The criterion is satisfiable only as an instantaneous measurement at t=1 ms.

evidence.locator: in-band time interval 0.9676-1.0498 ms; slope 0.368 mV/us at 1 ms

findings.mechanism: First-order RC with tau=1 ms rises monotonically toward the 1 V input; the band 0.62-0.65 V is occupied only during t in [0.9676, 1.0498] ms. Any reading of 'settles' as a steady-state requirement is unmeetable by this topology; any reading as a sampled value makes the result sensitive to the (unspecified) sampling instant at 0.368 mV/us.
findings.reasoning: Interpretation note for the adjudicator: under the instantaneous-sample reading the nominal design passes (CIR-1 evidence); under a steady-state reading no simple RC from a 1 V step can comply. Recorded at info level because the requirement wording, not the candidate hardware, is the source of ambiguity, and sampling timing is explicitly listed as unspecified.
findings.title: Output transits the window rather than settling; 'settles at 1 ms' is only an instantaneous sample

limitations: No ADC model was simulated: sampling capacitance, switch resistance, initial charge and sampling timing are unspecified by inputs/requirements.txt and the scope forbids inventing them; only bounding sensitivity calculations were performed
Component tolerance, temperature coefficient and capacitor DC-bias derating are not stated in the candidate, so only nominal values were evaluated; no Monte Carlo was run
PCB parasitics were estimated by inspection, not extracted; zone fill evaluated as saved (read-only candidate)
Connector J1 mating side (the actual ADC/source wiring) is outside the candidate and could not be checked for interface compatibility
